verdicts.misleading_risk: Low if limited to README order and hub text. Risk areas: (1) the auditor's claim that workflow-status Next goes to template-synchronization and loops back is FALSE (site/guides/workflow-status/index.html Next -> ../troubleshooting/; the site keeps only the first README occurrence of sync), and 'personal-access-token has no Next' is true but it is the last page, so harmless; do not repeat the loop claim. (2) Moving sync out of the early path (B2) and 'Accept a pull request' next to initialise changes the template's own hand-linked Previous/Next footers, which are written by hand in each .md (e.g. initialise_repository.md footer Next -> app_manifest.md, executable_creation.md footer Next -> download_executable.md), so README reorder alone would make the GitHub-side footers disagree with the order unless they are edited too. (3) A longer hubs.yaml flow is a second, hand-kept description of the path that can drift from the README.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Two small changes. Template repo (CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor, .tools/docs/README.md plus the footers of the pages that move): put accept_pull_request.md directly after initialise_repository.md in 'From zero to installed notebooks', and move installer_images.md, app_manifest.md, external_code_upload.md to after executable_creation.md (or into a short 'Customise (optional)' group); list template_synchronization.md once; fix the footers so GitHub readers see the same order. Site (labconstrictor-site data/hubs.yaml build.flow only, no code change): make the flow 5 steps that match the guides: Create repository, Initialise (guides/initialise-repository/), Add notebooks, Publish a release, Share it (submit/). Optionally a 'Start here' help line using the existing 'help' hub element (hubs.py write_hub already renders hub['help'] before the flow) linking guides/before-getting-started/; no new element needed. Do not add a separate pager list on the site. Note for the report: the hub already lists the groups in README order and the sidebar opens with 'Before getting started', so the gap is the pager and the 4-step flow, not a missing path. Drop the 'move the flow above the cards' idea (design choice, not a benchmark failure).
verdicts.evidence: Verified: site/guides/initialise-repository Next -> installer-images; notebook-upload Next -> executable-creation; executable-creation Next -> notebook-portability (template body footer says download_executable.md, which the site moved to the Use track, so the site pager jumps tracks' content); accept-pull-request is in 'GitHub management' (Previous use-cases, Next workflow-status). origin/main README.md lines 10-16 list installer_images, app_manifest, external_code_upload between initialise and requirements (the local checkout on branch claude/festive-cannon-epptr4 and local main are stale and lack these lines; the site is built from origin/main). docs/build/index.md and data/hubs.yaml: flow has 4 steps, step 2 links guides/notebook-upload/ and skips initialise. hubs.py:write_hub renders cards, then optional help, then flow. Built /build/ page: cards first, flow last. Refuted: workflow-status Next is troubleshooting, not template-synchronization.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. The auditor infers 'nothing in the first build depends on it' from sync_template.yml. That is mostly right (the token check step runs only if steps.version-check.outputs.sync_required == 'true', lines 115-132, and the failure message is explicit), but the maintainers made it a gate on purpose (commit ba9ec8e 'Include code and instructions to generate sync token'; template is already at 0.1.15, so a new repo will be asked to sync at the next release). Whether to keep it a gate is a product decision, not a docs defect. The 'Step 3 pre-0.1.12' point is correct for new repos (template_version 0.1.15), but troubleshooting.md already points to it. Proposing to say 'the weekly failure is harmless' would be an unverified claim: a failed scheduled run emails the owner and the workflow fails by design with ::error 'Synchronization setup required'. Time estimate would be invented unless someone times it.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Template repo only, docs-only, no workflow change: (a) in .tools/docs/README.md move template_synchronization.md out of the early path (list it once, in the 'GitHub management' group or right after executable_creation.md) and change the three gates to a one-line recommendation or drop them: create_repository.md line 34 section, initialise_repository.md line 9 note, before_getting_started.md line 37 clause; add one line under 'After the release' in executable_creation.md linking it. Only do this if the maintainers confirm sync can wait; if they want it early, keep the gate but add the stated reason in one sentence (new template versions are delivered as pull requests; without the token the scheduled run reports 'Synchronization setup required'). (b) Fix the wording 'the following video' -> 'the GIFs' (template_synchronization.md line 9). (c) Add a 'Check that it worked' line: Actions > Sync with Template Repository > Run workflow, and say what it prints when the repo is already up to date (verify by running it once before writing the sentence). (d) Leave Step 3 in place or move it to troubleshooting.md only if the page is kept short; do not add a time estimate unless measured. Lower priority than B3 and B4.
verdicts.evidence: Read .tools/docs/template_synchronization.md (Steps 1-3, GIF links, 'Follow the same instructions that are given in the following video' line 9), create_repository.md line 34 ('Before initialising the project, complete...'), origin/main initialise_repository.md line 9 note, before_getting_started.md line 37. sync_template.yml on: schedule weekly + workflow_dispatch; token check only when sync_required true. troubleshooting.md lines 18-42 already cover the missing/expired token and the pre-0.1.12 edit. workflow_status.md line 3 also states the token setup is required. .template_sync/manifest.yaml template_version 0.1.15.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium-high if the rewrite copies the form's labels and scope requirements into the guide without verifying them: the form is edited in another repository, so duplicated labels (Project icon image (resized to 256 x 256 px) etc.) will drift. The 'exact scopes' sentence is unverified (the streamlit code only checks the ghp_ prefix, app.py:972-977; I did not find what scopes the PR push needs; the form help text says 'repo permissions'). The personal_access_token.md 'Read-Only Access' section (classic token with 'Resource owner' and 'repo > contents') looks wrong for classic tokens, which do not offer a resource owner or a read-only repo scope, but I did not verify against live GitHub, so it should be checked by a maintainer before any text is written. 'Everything went well' (app.py:788) is the form's message and may change.
